name: decomposition
hypothesis: Formulating each decision field as narrow binary questions and reconstructing the field from independently calibrated binary probabilities beats the current flat multi-class head on held-out synthetic scenarios, measured on macro-F1 and on ECE. This is the decomposition move documented in docs/next-phase-plan.md B1.

arms.flat: one multi-class linear head per field over the versioned feature encoder (qc/training.py train_decision_provider)
arms.decomposed: one binary linear head per narrow question: one-vs-rest for nominal fields, threshold decomposition for the ordinal severity field. Fields are reconstructed from the binary probabilities (qc/decomposition.py).

design.held_constant: identical feature encoder and FEATURE_VERSION, identical frozen train/validation/test split, identical optimizer budget (epochs, learning_rate, l2). Only the target formulation differs.

questions.likely_cause: 12 one-vs-rest noul questions, one per declared cause value
questions.likely_origin: 6 one-vs-rest noul questions, one per declared origin value
questions.severity: 3 threshold noul questions (>= MEDIUM, >= HIGH, >= CRITICAL) reconstructed as an ordinal distribution

splits.grouping: incident_group = scenario_id, so sibling runs of one scenario cannot straddle a split while families remain represented on both sides

analysis: Point estimate of decomposed minus flat on the frozen test split, with a paired bootstrap 95% interval over test scenarios (2000 resamples, seed 0). Reported per field and overall. A failed gate is reported as failed; no fallback arm is substituted and no threshold is moved after the fact.
eligibility: synthetic only. Passing this gate can never confer production_eligible; that requires a pinned real test artifact and operational checks (docs/claims.md).
